dish: Hainanese chicken rice, soup, chilli and dark soy
read: One oval dish of sliced poached chicken, about 8 slices and 125 g of meat. One moulded dome of chicken rice, 160 g. A bowl of clear soup. Two small dips. Singapore's composition table puts one plate of steamed Hainanese chicken rice at 600 kcal and 33 g of protein, which the catalogue also holds, and the soup and dips are the rest.

dish: Nasi lemak with fried chicken, pork chop, egg and sambal
read: Coconut rice about 180 g, one bone-in fried chicken quarter at roughly 110 g of meat, a fried egg, a slab of pork chop about 80 g, two or three fried fritters, a vegetable kerabu and a cup of sambal. The one plate here where the breakdown is close.

dish: Pork belly with green peppers, omelette and rice
read: Three shared dishes photographed together: a whole cut omelette of two or three eggs, a plate of stir-fried pork belly with green peppers, and a small bowl of PLAIN white rice, not fried. Pork belly is about 13 g of protein per 100 g and mostly fat, so a plate of it cannot be 40% protein by energy.

dish: Hainanese chicken rice, soup, chilli and dark soy
read: The same lunch as 01, photographed twice and cropped differently. Two readings of one meal are worth having: they measure how much of the answer is the pipeline and how much is the framing.

dish: Boxed nasi lemak with fried chicken
read: A takeaway box: rice about 160 g, one fried chicken thigh at roughly 85 g of meat off the bone, fried anchovies and shallots, a cabbage leaf, a cucumber slice, a cup of gravy.

dish: Karaage with potato salad, rice and soup
read: About 180 g of fried chicken, a scoop of potato salad, a generous blob of mayonnaise, pickled radish, a full bowl of white rice and a bowl of soup. The mayonnaise is a quarter of the calories and the easiest thing on the plate to miss, which is why this case is here.
Restaurant tagliatelle, about 180 g cooked, with four or five large shell-on prawns yielding roughly 100 g of meat, oil and arugula. Prawn shells and heads are on the plate and are not food.

dish: Rolled omelette with rice and prawn curry
read: Four slices of rolled omelette with a meat filling, about 130 g. A modest heap of plain white rice, about 140 g. A tub of prawn sambal with onions, about 150 g including the oil.

dish: Fried beehoon with fried chicken and fried sides
read: A takeaway plate of fried beehoon about 150 g, one fried chicken thigh at roughly 80 g of meat, two spring rolls, three fritter discs and a handful of battered vegetable fritters. Almost everything is fried, so the calories are high and the protein is not.

dish: Karaage with cream sauce, potatoes, rice and soup
read: About 180 g of fried chicken under a heavy tartar-style cream sauce, potato wedges, a bowl of white rice and a soup. Fried chicken with cream sauce is a FAT dish: the pipeline priced this part at 100 g of carbohydrate, which is the same wrong-row failure as the protein cases wearing a different macro.

dish: Claypot rice with sliced beef and minced meat
read: A claypot of rice, about 250 g, topped with roughly 80 g of sliced beef, 60 g of minced meat and an egg yolk, with a side of edamame and a dipping sauce. The pipeline priced the rice part at 380 g and 25 g of protein, which is the whole pot with the meat already in it, and then added the meat again.
